notes: Machine-readable freeze of RELATE v0.1 section 3 (relations), section 2 (domains), section 4 (relevance grades), section 5 (overlap bands), section 6 (hard-negative methods). Changing anything here is a MINOR version bump and must be recorded in spec/RELATE-CHANGELOG.md.

relations.definition: a and b express the same proposition; a entails b and b entails a; truth-conditionally identical.
relations.decision_procedure: Could a careful reader be shown one then the other and say 'that's the same statement, reworded'? Swapping them in any factual context changes nothing.

relations.direction_meaning: b is the explicit negation of a
relations.definition: b is a with the main predicate explicitly negated (surface 'not', 'no', 'never', 'fails to'), minimal other change; high lexical overlap by construction. A lexically-closest subset of contradiction.
relations.decision_procedure: Can b be produced from a by inserting/removing a negation on the main verb or a core quantifier, changing little else?

constraints.lexical_overlap_min_reason: spec 3.6 - a low-overlap 'negation' is mislabeled and should be 'contradiction'

relations.direction_meaning: b has a's entities and relation type with the argument roles reversed
relations.definition: b contains the same entities and same relation type as a but with argument roles reversed (A acquired B -> B acquired A; X is north of Y -> Y is north of X).
relations.decision_procedure: Same entities, same relation predicate, arguments swapped. Always also a contradiction when the relation is asymmetric.

relations.definition: a and b cannot both be true in the same world; at least one atomic claim is directly negated or made incompatible (mutually exclusive values, incompatible relations). Distinct from negation: contradiction may be lexically diverse.
relations.decision_procedure: Is there NO consistent world containing both? If both can be true at different times AND both carry/imply a time index, it is temporal-mismatch, not contradiction.

relations.direction_meaning: b is a at a different (usually later) time
relations.definition: a and b state the same relation about the same entity with different, time-dependent values; each is (or was) true at its own time; the mismatch is only temporal.
relations.decision_procedure: Same subject, same relation, values differ, difference explained by 'measured at different times'. Requires both items to carry or plausibly imply a time.

relations.direction_meaning: a entails b, and NOT b entails a (strict one-directional)
relations.definition: Every situation making a true makes b true; the reverse fails.
relations.decision_procedure: Assume a: is b guaranteed? Assume b: is a still possibly false? Both yes -> entailment(a->b). If the reverse also holds it is paraphrase/equivalent.

relations.definition: b provides evidence for some but not all of a; b neither entails nor contradicts a; a reader using b to check a would say 'supports part of this, silent on the rest'.
relations.decision_procedure: Decompose a into atomic claims. Does b entail at least one and leave at least one unaddressed (not contradicted)?

relations.definition: Same core meaning, possibly differing in emphasis, register, or non-truth-conditional detail; mutual entailment holds for the salient claim but one side may carry minor extra or softened content. If mutual entailment is exact and total -> equivalent instead.
relations.decision_procedure: Same event/claim, different words; a reader accepts 'these say basically the same thing' but not necessarily 'identical'.

relations.definition: a and b concern the same topic or event but make different, logically independent claims (neither entails, contradicts, nor partially supports the other).
relations.decision_procedure: Shared topic, independent claims, none of the higher-precedence relations apply.

relations.definition: a and b share at least one named entity but are about different topics/claims and are not topic-related in a strong sense.
relations.decision_procedure: Shared entity only; different topic; none of the higher-precedence relations apply.

relations.definition: No shared topic, no shared salient entity, no logical relation. Often cross-domain.
relations.decision_procedure: A reader says 'these have nothing to do with each other'.

hard_negative.definition: A role tag on a (query, candidate) pair meaning the candidate is highly similar to the query under lexical/topical/entity signals but is NOT a correct answer. Every hard negative also carries its underlying base relation.

relevance_grades.3: answers the query and is correct (equivalent / paraphrase / forward entailment to the query claim, and true)
relevance_grades.2: substantially supports the query (partial-support covering the main claim)
relevance_grades.0: everything else (entity-related, contradiction, negation, temporal-mismatch, unrelated) - contradiction/negation get 0 by design, making RELATE a polarity probe
